text:
Oliver Bjorkstrand landed in New York after a season in Tampa Bay, and the Rangers have found a use for him: 7 goals and 11 points in 22 games on fewer than 12 minutes a night. Three of those points have come on the power play, including the goal NHL.com and CBS Sports logged on Nov. 14.

The goals are running ahead of the chances, by about two and a half, so we'd expect the scoring rate to cool. His minutes are up more than two a night over the last ten games. The Rangers get about 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, a bit better than without him.

That's a turnaround from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him barely above replacement and his team's chance creation in the bottom 10% of forwards with him on the ice; nearly all his value then came on the power play. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on only 35% of his entries. Watch whether the extra ice time holds when the shooting luck runs out.
